the results from this study are consistent with the hypothesis that the consumption of dietary fat, especially in the form of saturated fatty acids (SFA) and trans fatty acids (TFA), is associated with an increased risk for developing type 2 diabetes, whereas the consumption of dietary carbohydrates is inversely associated with this risk.
